posts.title: US lawmakers near deal to ban Chinese cars with carve-out for Mercedes, report says
posts.summary:
Lawmakers in Washington are aiming to send the bill to Trump by the end of the year, according to Bloomberg.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: US lawmakers are negotiating a bill to ban Chinese-made vehicles from the US market, with the goal of sending legislation to President Trump by year-end.
The proposed bill aims to address national security concerns regarding data transmission in connected vehicles, potentially impacting automakers with significant Chinese ownership.
Negotiations include a potential carve-out for Mercedes-Benz, reflecting the complexity of balancing security restrictions with the interests of global automakers.

posts.title: What a billion-dollar deal says about the US battery market
posts.summary: After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US. Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries. It’s a deal that Sila says could be worth more than…
bullets: Sila's silicon-carbon anode material offers significant performance gains, including a 50% reduction in volume and 80% reduction in weight compared to traditional graphite anodes.
The deal with Panasonic Energy marks Sila's first mass-market agreement, aiming to scale production by at least 10 times current levels.

The project is heavily supported by a $1.4 billion loan from the U.S. Defense Department, highlighting a shift in battery manufacturing focus toward national security and domestic supply chain resilience.
This partnership represents a critical milestone for the U.S. next-generation battery market, which has struggled with high-profile failures in recent years.

posts.title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
posts.summary:
Moving voltage regulators closer to processors can reduce power loss, but adds challenges for advanced packaging, thermal management, and system-level design.
The post AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: AI accelerators running at 600W+ require currents exceeding 1,000 amps, forcing a shift toward vertical power delivery networks to mitigate resistive losses and voltage droop.
Designers are increasingly moving voltage regulator modules (VRMs) from the PCB periphery to the package interposer or directly onto the silicon to reduce IR drop.
The transition from discrete PMICs to distributed integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) necessitates complex system-level co-design of passives, interposers, and power management circuitry.

posts.title: An Interview With Eric Seufert About Agentic Commerce
posts.summary: An interview with Eric Seufert about agentic commerce, including why he thinks ads will be the answer, and why I want retailers who cater to agents.
bullets: The discussion explores the emergence of 'agentic commerce,' where autonomous AI agents perform shopping tasks on behalf of consumers.
Eric Seufert argues that digital advertising will remain the primary monetization model for these agent-driven platforms, rather than being displaced by them.
The analysis highlights a strategic shift for retailers, who must now optimize their digital presence to cater to AI agents rather than just human users.
This transition suggests a fundamental change in the customer acquisition funnel, as agents prioritize efficiency and data-driven purchasing over traditional brand marketing.
